## Course Goals

By the end of this course, you should be able to:

1. Have a general understanding of the current applications of genAI tools in sociological research, and form your own evaluations on their effectiveness
2. Understand how you can incorporate genAI tools for your own research interests
3. Understand what genAI can and cannot do for producing high-quality research

## Final Project: Three Tracks

Your project must fulfill **at least one** of:

1. The research **uses genAI/LLM** as part of its research methods
2. The research is **about** the usage or applications of genAI/LLM
3. The research **tests/pilots** genAI/LLM tools for the research workflow

. . .

**Deliverables:**

- Types (1) or (2): project proposal, ≥8 pages (double-spaced, 12pt)
- Type (3): project report (~5 pp.) + reflection (~5 pp.) + code/appendix

**Timeline:** Co-work on Weeks 4 & 6 → Presentations on Week 7

## AI Usage Policy

::: {.callout-important}
## AI writing is strictly banned

You are **not allowed** to use AI to generate any writing assignments for this course.
:::

**Permitted:**

- Grammar corrections only (subject–verb agreement, tense, articles, spelling)
- Using genAI as a **research tool** in labs and projects

**Rule of thumb:** Do not automate the process of learning, thinking, and writing.

You are held responsible for your research design and every analytical decision, regardless of whether it is made by you or your AI agents.

# Part II: State of GenAI in Social Science Research {.center background-color="#CC0033"}

*2:45–3:30*

## What is Generative AI?

**Generative AI** = models that produce new content — text, images, video, code, audio — rather than classifying or scoring existing data.

. . .

**Types of generative models:**

- **Text generation:** LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, Llama, Gemini, DeepSeek)
- **Image generation:** DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion
- **Video generation:** Sora, Runway, Kling
- **Multimodal:** models that handle text + images + video together

## Frontier Models & Open-Weight Models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Frontier (proprietary) models:**

- [OpenAI GPT-4o / o1](https://openai.com)
- [Anthropic Claude](https://anthropic.com)
- [Google Gemini](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/)
- [xAI Grok](https://x.ai)

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Open-weight models:**

- [Meta Llama](https://llama.meta.com/)
- [DeepSeek](https://www.deepseek.com/)
- [Mistral](https://mistral.ai/)
- [Qwen](https://qwenlm.github.io/)

:::
::::

. . .

The distinction matters for research: open-weight models allow inspection and fine-tuning; proprietary models offer higher capability but less transparency.

## Engage & Share

**Discussion:**

- Which AI models have you tried?
- What tasks do you ask them to do?
- How "good" are they for your purposes?
- What surprised you — or disappointed you?

## Ongoing Debates

These developments raise hard questions:

::: {.incremental}
- **Ethics of AI use** — Where is the line between augmentation and academic dishonesty?
- **Integrity of academic work** — If an LLM co-writes your paper, whose ideas are they?
- **Inequality in knowledge production** — Does AI lower barriers for some (language, training) while reinforcing them for others (access, resources, normative orientations)?
- **Quality of AI-generated research** — Can automated pipelines produce genuinely novel insights?
:::

<!-- TODO: optional — show screenshot of recent Nature/Science articles on AI & science -->

## GenAI in Sociological Research

### Pre-AI computational methods:

- Dictionary methods, topic modeling, word embeddings
- Named entity recognition, dependency parsing
- Supervised ML classifiers, agent-based models
- **Research goals:** measuring sentiments, identifying themes, quantifying meanings, extracting information and relations, classifying text

## GenAI in Sociological Research (cont.)

### After AI, three shifts:

::: {.incremental}
1. **Same goals, new tools** — Tasks like annotation (sentiment, themes, classification, information extraction) can now be performed by LLMs/MLLMs without developing specialized algorithms
2. **Expanded scope** — AI enables new scales and modalities: large-scale image annotation, customized survey follow-up questions, simulated social interactions
3. **New research topics** — AI as surrogates for human populations, biases in AI, AI and scientific knowledge production, human-AI interaction, social and ethical implications (labor markets, monopoly, environmental politics of AI, etc.)
:::

## This Course's Focus

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
**This minicourse** focuses mainly on:

- **(2) GenAI as research methods** — annotation, simulation, autoresearch, qualitative analysis
- **AI as surrogates** from (3) — how well do LLMs mirror human populations?
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Coming next:** In the follow-up minicourse *Sociology of AI*, we focus on **(3)** — the social, ethical, and political dimensions of AI as a technology.
:::
::::

## Lab Overview

Today's lab covers:

1. **Data management rules** — the 3-2-1 rule, sandbox environments for AI co-work
2. **Version control** — what Git is and why we need it
3. **CLI basics** — where to find it, why we need it
4. **Python** — what it is, how it compares to R
5. **Conda** — managing environments and packages
6. **Jupyter Notebook** — what it is, notebooks vs. scripts
7. **Basic data wrangling & ML in Python** — loading data, descriptives, supervised & unsupervised models
